metadata.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow

nodes.name: The Transport Mapping Problem
nodes.statement: \textbf{The Transport Mapping Problem} \emph{Given empirical observations of two distributions $X_0\sim \tg_0,  X_1\sim \tg_1$ on $\RR^d$, find a transport map $T\colon\RR^d\to\RR^d$ (hopefully nice or optimal in certain sense), such that $Z_1 \defeq T(Z_0)\sim \tg_1$ when $Z_0 \sim \tg_0$, that is, $(Z_0,Z_1)$ is a coupling (a.k.a transport plan) of $\tg_0$ and $\tg_1$.}
assumptions: empirical observations of two distributions $X_0\sim \tg_0,  X_1\sim \tg_1$ on $\RR^d$
conclusions: find a transport map $T\colon\RR^d\to\RR^d$ (hopefully nice or optimal in certain sense), such that $Z_1 \defeq T(Z_0)\sim \tg_1$ when $Z_0 \sim \tg_0$, that is, $(Z_0,Z_1)$ is a coupling (a.k.a transport plan) of $\tg_0$ and $\tg_1$.

nodes.name: Expected velocity $v^\X$
nodes.statement: For a path-wise continuously differentiable random process  $\X = \{X_t\colon t\in[0,1]\}$, its expected velocity $v^\X$ is defined as $$v^\X(x, t) = \E[\dot X_t ~|~ X_t = x],~~~~~ \forall x\in \supp(X_t). $$ For $x\not\in \supp(X_t)$, the conditional expectation is not defined and we set $v^\X$ arbitrarily, say $v^\X(x,t) = 0$.

nodes.name: Rectifiable process; rectified flow induced from $\vv X$
nodes.statement: We call that $\vv X$ is rectifiable if $v^\X$ is locally bounded and the solution of the integral equation below exists and  is unique: \bbb  Z_t = Z_0 + \int_0^t v^\X(Z_t, t) \dt,~~~~\forall t\in[0,1],~~~~ Z_0 = X_0. \eee In this case, $\vv Z = \{Z_t\colon t\in[0,1]\}$ is called the rectified flow induced from $\vv X$.

nodes.name: Rectifiable coupling; rectified coupling
nodes.statement: A coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ is called rectifiable if its linear interpolation process $\vv X = \{tX_1+(1-t)X_0\colon t\in[0,1]\}$ is rectifiable. In this case, the $\vv Z=\{Z_t\colon t \in[0,1]\}$ in \eqref{equ:znonlinear} is called the rectified flow of coupling $(X_0,X_1)$, denoted as $\vv Z = \rectifyflow((X_0,X_1))$, and $(Z_0,Z_1)$ is called the rectified coupling of $(X_0,X_1)$, denoted as $(Z_0,Z_1) = \rectify((X_0,X_1)).$

nodes.name: Straight (fully rectified) coupling
nodes.statement: A coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ is said to be straight (or fully rectified)  if it is a fixed point of the $\rectify(\cdot)$ mapping.

nodes.name: $c$-optimal coupling
nodes.statement: A coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ is called $c$-optimal if it achieves the minimum of $\E[c(X_1-X_0)]$ among all couplings that share the same marginals.

nodes.name: Straight flow
nodes.statement: we say that a flow $\d Z_t = v(Z_t, t)\dt$ is straight if we have almost surely that $Z_t = t Z_1 + (1-t) Z_0$ for $\forall t\in[0,1]$, or equivalently $v(Z_t,t)=Z_1-Z_0=\const$ following each path.

nodes.name: Marginal preserving property (Theorem 3.3)
nodes.statement: Assume $\vv X$ is rectifiable and $\vv Z$ is its rectified flow. Then  $\law(Z_t) =\law(X_t)$ for $\forall t\in[0,1]$.
assumptions: $\vv X$ is rectifiable and $\vv Z$ is its rectified flow

nodes.name: Reducing convex transport costs (Theorem 3.5)
nodes.statement: Assume $(X_0,X_1)$ is rectifiable and $(Z_0,Z_1) = \rectify((X_0,X_1))$. Then for any convex function $c\colon \RR^d\to \RR$, we have $$\E[c(Z_1 - Z_0)] \leq \E[c(X_1 - X_0)].$$

nodes.name: Characterization of straight couplings (Theorem 3.6)
nodes.statement: Assume $(X_0,X_1)$ is rectifiable. Let $X_t =  tX_1 +(1-t)X_0$ and $\vv Z =\rectifyflow((X_0,X_1))$. Then $(X_0,X_1)$ is a straight coupling iff the following equivalent statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item There exists a strictly convex function $c\colon \RR^d\to \RR$, such that $\E[c(Z_1-Z_0)] = \E[c(X_1-X_0)]$. \item $(X_0,X_1)$ is a fixed point of $\rectify(\cdot)$, that is, $(X_0,X_1) = (Z_0,Z_1)$. \item The rectified flow coincides with the linear interpolation process: $\vv X = \vv Z$. \item The paths of the linear interpolation $\vv X$ do not intersect: \bbb V((X_0,X_1)):= \int_0^1 \e{\norm{X_1-X_0-\e{X_1-X_0~|~X_t}}^2} \dt = 0, \eee where $V((X_0,X_1))=0$ indicates that $X_1-X_0=\E[X_1-X_0|X_t]$ almost surely when $t\sim \uniform([0,1])$, meaning that the lines passing through each $X_t$ is unique, and hence no linear interpolation paths intersect. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: $(X_0,X_1)$ is a straight coupling iff the following equivalent statements hold (Statements 1--4)

nodes.name: $\bigO{1/K}$ convergence rate (Theorem 3.7)
nodes.statement: Let $\vv Z^k$ the $k$-th rectified flow of $(X_0,X_1)$, that is, $\vv Z^{k+1} = \rectifyflow((Z_0^k, Z_1^k))$ and $(Z_0^0,Z_1^0) = (X_0,X_1)$. Assume each $(Z_0^k,Z_1^k)$ is rectifiable for $k=0,\ldots, K$. Then \bb \sum_{k=0}^K S(\vv Z^{k+1}) + V( (Z^k_0, Z^k_1)) \leq  \e{\norm{X_1-X_0}^2}. \ee
assumptions: $\vv Z^k$ the $k$-th rectified flow of $(X_0,X_1)$, that is, $\vv Z^{k+1} = \rectifyflow((Z_0^k, Z_1^k))$ and $(Z_0^0,Z_1^0) = (X_0,X_1)$

nodes.name: $c$-optimal implies straight (Theorem 3.8)
nodes.statement: If a rectifiable  coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ is $c$-optimal for some strictly convex cost function $c$, then $(X_0,X_1)$ is a straight coupling.
assumptions: a rectifiable  coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ is $c$-optimal for some strictly convex cost function $c$

nodes.name: Straight couplings on $\RR$ (Theorem 3.10)
nodes.statement: For any $\tg_0,\tg_1$ on $\RR$, there exists either no straight coupling, or a unique straight coupling. Further, if exists, the unique straight coupling is  deterministic and monotonic,  and jointly optimal w.r.t. all  convex cost functions $c\colon \RR^d\to [0,+\infty)$ for which the minimum value of $\e{c(X_1-X_0)}$ exists and is finite.
conclusions: there exists either no straight coupling, or a unique straight coupling

if exists, the unique straight coupling is  deterministic and monotonic,  and jointly optimal w.r.t. all  convex cost functions $c\colon \RR^d\to [0,+\infty)$ for which the minimum value of $\e{c(X_1-X_0)}$ exists and is finite

nodes.name: Straight iff deterministic and monotonic (Lemma 3.9)
nodes.statement: A coupling on $\RR$ is  straight iff it is deterministic and monotonic.
conclusions: is  straight iff it is deterministic and monotonic

nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{equ:alphadiff} hold. Then \eqref{equ:odeobjgg} is equivalent to \eqref{equ:Lgvphi} with $X_t = \alpha_t X_1 + \betatogamma_t \xi$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3 (marginal preserving)
nodes.statement: For any compactly supported continuously differentiable test function $h\colon \RR^d\to \RR$, we have \bbb  \ddt \E[h(X_t)] = \E[\dd h(X_t)\tt \dot X_t ] = \E[\dd h(X_t)\tt v^\X(X_t,t)], \eee where we used  $v^\X(X_t,t) = \E[\dot X_t |X_t]$. By definition, this is equivalent to that $\tg_t \defeq \law(X_t)$ solves in the sense of distributions the continuity equation with drift $v_t^\X \defeq v^\X(\cdot,t)$: \bbb \dot \tg_t + \div (v_t^\X \tg_t) = 0. \eee To see the equivalence of \eqref{equ:ehxt} and \eqref{equ:contieq}, we can multiply \eqref{equ:contieq} with $h$ and integrate both sides: \bb 0 = \int h(\dot \tg_t + \div (v_t^\X \tg_t)) = \int h \dot \tg_t - \dd h\tt v_t^\X \tg_t =  \ddt  \E[h(X_t) ]  - \E[\dd h(X_t)\tt v^\X(X_t,t)], \ee where we use integration by parts that $\int h\div (v^\X_t \tg_t)= - \int \dd h\tt (v^\X_t \tg_t)$. Because $Z_t$ is driven by the same velocity field $v^\X$, its  marginal law $\law(Z_t)$ solves the very same equation with the same initial condition ($Z_0=X_0$). Hence,  the equivalence of $\law(Z_t)$ and $\law(X_t)$ follows if the solution of \eqref{equ:contieq} is unique, which is equivalent to the uniqueness of the solution of $\d Z_t = \vofX(Z_t,t)$ following Corollary 1.3 of \citet{kurtz2011equivalence} (see also Theorem 4.1 of \citet{ambrosio2008existence}).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.5 (cost reduction via Jensen)
nodes.statement: The proof is based on elementary applications of Jensen's inequality. \bb \E\left [c(Z_1 - Z_0)\right] & = \E \left[ c\left(\int_0^1 \vofX(Z_t, t) \dt\right) \right ]  \ant{as $\d Z_t = \vofX(Z_t,t)\dt$}\\ &\leq \E \left[ \int_0^1 c \left (\vofX(Z_t, t)  \right) \dt \right ]  \ant{convexity of $c$, Jensen's inequality}\\ & = \E \left[ \int_0^1 c \left( \vofX(X_t, t)  \right) \dt \right ]  \ant{$X_t$ and $Z_t$ shares the same marginals}\\ & =  \E \left[ \int_0^1 c\left ( \E\left [(X_1-X_0)~|~X_t \right ] \right) \dt \right ] \ant{definition of $\vofX$}\\ & \leq  \E \left[ \int_0^1  \E\left [ c\left(X_1-X_0 \right) |~X_t \right ]   \dt \right ] \ant{convexity of $c$, Jensen's inequality}\\ & = \int_0^1\E\left [c\left(X_1 - X_0\right)\right] \dt  \ant{$\E[\E[(X_1-X_0) | X_t]] = \E[(X_1-X_0)]$}\\ & = \E\left [c\left (X_1 - X_0 \right) \right]. \ee

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.6 (equivalence of straightness statements)
nodes.statement: $3 \to 2\to 1$: Obvious. $1\to 4$: If $\E[c(Z_1-Z_0)] = \E[c(X_1-X_0)]$, the two applications of Jensen's inequality in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:cost} are tight. Because $c$ is strictly convex, the second Jensen's inequality in the proof implies that $X_1-X_0 = \E[X_1-X_0~|~X_t]$ almost surely w.r.t. $X$ and $t\sim \uniform([0,1]),$ which implies that $V(\vv X)=0.$ $4\to 3$: If $V(\vv X) =0$, we have $\int_0^s( X_1 -X_0) \dt = \int_0^s\E[X_1-X_0|X_t]\dt = \int_0^sv^X(X_t,t)\dt $ for $s\in(0,1]$. Hence \bb X_t = X_0 +\int_0^t (X_1-X_0) \dt = X_0 + \int_0^t v^X(X_t, t) \dt. \ee Because $\vv Z$ satisfies the same equation \eqref{equ:znonlinear}, we have $\vv X=\vv Z$ by the uniqueness of the solution.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.7 (telescoping convergence)
Proof of Theorem 3.8 ($c$-optimal implies straight)
nodes.statement: Let $(Z_0,Z_1) = \rectify((X_0,X_1))$. If $(X_0,X_1)$ is $c$-optimal, we must have $\E[c(Z_1-Z_0)] = \E[c(X_1-X_0)]$. This implies Statement 1 in Theorem \ref{thm:straightness} and hence that $(X_0,X_1)$ is straight.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.9 (straight iff deterministic monotonic)
nodes.statement: If $(X_0,X_1)$ on $\RR$ is straight, then it coincides with its rectified coupling $(Z_0,Z_1) = \rectify((X_0,X_1)).$ But because $(Z_0,Z_1)$ is induced from the rectified flow $\d Z_t = v^X(Z_t, t) \dt $, it is obviously deterministic. It is also monotonic due to the non-crossing property of flows.  Specifically, if $(Z_0,Z_1)$ is not monotonic, there exists $(z_0,z_1)$ and $(z_0',z_1')$ in the support of $(Z_0,Z_1)$ such that $z_0<z_0'$ and $z_1 > z_1'$. If this happens, there must exists $t_0\in(0,1)$, such that $z_{t_0} = z_{t_0}'$. But by the uniqueness of the solution, we have $z_t=z_t$ for $t\geq t_0$, which is conflicting with $z_1 > z_1'$. Assume $(X_0,X_1)$ is deterministic and monotonic. Due to the monotonicity, there exists no $x_0$ and $x_0'$ in the support of $\tg_0$, such that $x_0 \neq x_0'$ and $x_{t_0} = x_{t_0}'$ for some $t_0<1$.  This suggests that $X_1-X_0 = \E[X_1-X_0~|~X_t] = v^X(X_t,t)$ for $t\in(0,1)$, and hence  $\d  X_t = (X_1-X_0)\dt = v^X(X_t) \dt $, which is the ODE of the rectified flow. In addition, $X_t$ is obviously the unique solution of this ODE.  Hence $(X_0,X_1)$ is rectifiable and straight following Statement 3 of Theorem~\ref{thm:straightness}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.10 (1D straight coupling)
nodes.statement: This is the result of Lemma~\ref{thm:monostraightlemma} combined with the fact that the monotonic coupling is unique and jointly optimal for all convex $c$ for which the optimal coupling exists, following Lemma 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 of \cite{santambrogio2015optimal}.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.11 (PF-ODE equivalence)
nodes.section: 3.5 Denoising Diffusion Models and Probability Flow ODEs
nodes.statement: First, note that we can take $\xi_t = \xi$ for all time $t$, as the correlation structure of $\xi_t$ does not impact the result. Hence, we have $V_t = X_t = \alpha_t X_1 + \beta_t \xi$. To show the equivalence of \eqref{equ:odeobjgg} and \eqref{equ:Lgvphi}, we just need to verify that $\dot X_t = \tilde Y_t$. \bb \tilde Y_t & = -\eta_t X_t + \frac{\sigma_t^2}{2\betatogamma_t^2} ( \alpha_t X_1 - X_t) \\ & = -\dot \eta_t \left ( \alpha_t X_1 + \betatogamma_t \xi \right) + \frac{\sigma_t^2}{2\betatogamma_t}  \xi \\ & = - \dot \eta \alpha_t X_1 + \left ( - \dot \eta_t \betatogamma_t + \frac{\sigma_t^2}{2\betatogamma_t} \right ) \xi \\ & \overset{(*)}{=} \dot \alpha_t X_1 +  \dot \betatogamma_t \xi \\ & = \dot X_t. \ee where in $\overset{(*)}{=}$ we used that $\eta_t = - \frac{\dot \alpha_t}{\alpha_t}$ and $ {\sigma_t^2} = 2\betatogamma_t^2  \left (\frac{\dot\alpha_t}{\alpha_t} -\frac{\dot \betatogamma_t}{\betatogamma_t} \right )$ which can be derived from \eqref{equ:alphadiff}.

nodes.name: Rectified Flow: Main Algorithm
input: Draws from a coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ of $\tg_0$ and $\tg_1$
nodes.statement: \STATE \textbf{Procedure}: $\vv Z={\rectifyflow((X_0,X_1))}$: \STATE~~~\emph{Inputs}: Draws from a coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ of $\tg_0$ and $\tg_1$; velocity model $v_\theta \colon \RR^d \to \RR^d$ with parameter $\theta.$ \STATE~~\emph{Training}: $\displaystyle \hat \theta = \argmin_\theta \E\left [\norm{X_1 - X_0 - v(t X_1 +(1-t)X_0, ~t )}^2 \right], $ with $t \sim \uniform([0,1])$. \STATE~~\emph{Sampling}: Draw $(Z_0,Z_1)$ following $\d Z_t = v_{\hat\theta}(Z_t,t)\dt$ starting from $Z_0 \sim \tg_0$ (or backwardly $Z_1\sim \tg_1$). \STATE~~\emph{Return}: $\vv Z = \{Z_t\colon t\in[0,1]\}$. \STATE \textbf{Reflow} (optional): $\vv Z^{k+1} = \rectifyflow((Z_0^k, Z_1^k))$, starting from $(Z^0_0,Z^0_1) = (X_0,X_1)$. \STATE \textbf{Distill} (optional): Learn a neural network $\hat T$ to distill the $k$-rectified flow, such that $Z^k_1 \approx \hat T(Z^k_0)$.

nodes.name: Train(Data)
nodes.statement: \PyInput{Input: Data=\{x0, x1\}} \\ \PyInput{Output: Model $v(x,t)$ for the rectified flow} \\ \PyCode{initialize Model} \\ \PyCode{for x0, x1 in Data:} \PyComment{x0, x1:~samples from  $\tg_0$,  $\tg_1$} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Optimizer.zero\_grad()} \\ \PyCode{~~~~t = torch.rand(batchsize)}~~\PyComment{Randomly sample  $t \in$ [0,1]} \\ \PyCode{~~~~\blue{Loss = ( Model(t*x1+(1-t)*x0,~t) - (x1-x0) ).pow(2).mean()}} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Loss.backward()} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Optimizer.step()} \\ \PyCode{return Model}

nodes.name: Sample(Model, Data)
nodes.statement: \PyInput{Input: Model $v(x,t)$ of the rectified flow} \\ \PyInput{Output: draws of the rectified coupling $(Z_0,Z_1)$} \\ \PyCode{coupling = []} \\ \PyCode{for x0, \_ in Data:} \PyComment{x0:~samples from  $\tg_0$ (batchsize$\times$dim)} \\ \PyCode{~~~~x1 = model.ODE\_solver(x0)} \\ \PyCode{~~~~coupling.append((x0, x1))} \\ \PyCode{return coupling}

nodes.name: Reflow(Data)
nodes.statement: \PyInput{Input: Data=\{x0, x1\}} \\ \PyInput{Output: draws of the $K$-th rectified coupling} \\ \PyCode{Coupling = Data} \\ \PyCode{for  $k=1,\ldots,K$:} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Model = Train(Coupling)} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Coupling = sample(Model, Data)} \\ \PyCode{return Coupling}

nodes.name: Rectified flow least-squares objective
nodes.statement: \min_{v} \int_0^1\E \left [ \norm{( X_1 - X_0) - v\big (X_t,~ t\big)}^2 \right ] \dt, ~~~~~\text{with}~~~~ X_t = t X_1 + (1-t) X_0,

nodes.name: Closed-form velocity field $v^X$
nodes.statement: v^X(z,t) = \e{\frac{X_1-z}{1-t} \eta_t(X_1, z)}, && \eta_t(X_1, z) = {\rho\left (\frac{z-t X_1}{1-t} ~\bigg |~X_1 \right )}\bigg  /{\e{\rho\left (\frac{z-t X_1}{1-t} ~\bigg |~X_1\right )}},

nodes.name: Straightness measure $S(\traj Z)$
nodes.statement: S(\traj Z) = \int_0^1 \e{\norm{(Z_1-Z_0) -\dot Z_t}^2} \dt.

nodes.name: Nonlinear rectified flow objective
nodes.statement: \min_{v} \int_0^1 \e{ w_t \norm{v(X_t, ~t) - \ddtdot X_t }^2}   \dt ,

nodes.name: Per-step identity from Theorem 3.5 proof
Apply to each rectification step
nodes.statement: Applying it to each rectification step yields $$ \E\left [\norm{Z^k_1-Z^k_0}^2\right ] - \E\left [\norm{Z^{k+1}_1-Z^{k+1}_0}^2\right ] = S(\vv Z^{k+1}) + V((Z_0^k,Z_1^k)). $$

nodes.name: Telescoping sum
nodes.statement: A telescoping sum on $k=0,\ldots, K$ gives the result.

nodes.name: Straight $\Rightarrow$ deterministic and monotonic
nodes.statement: If $(X_0,X_1)$ on $\RR$ is straight, then it coincides with its rectified coupling $(Z_0,Z_1) = \rectify((X_0,X_1)).$ But because $(Z_0,Z_1)$ is induced from the rectified flow $\d Z_t = v^X(Z_t, t) \dt $, it is obviously deterministic. It is also monotonic due to the non-crossing property of flows.  Specifically, if $(Z_0,Z_1)$ is not monotonic, there exists $(z_0,z_1)$ and $(z_0',z_1')$ in the support of $(Z_0,Z_1)$ such that $z_0<z_0'$ and $z_1 > z_1'$. If this happens, there must exists $t_0\in(0,1)$, such that $z_{t_0} = z_{t_0}'$. But by the uniqueness of the solution, we have $z_t=z_t$ for $t\geq t_0$, which is conflicting with $z_1 > z_1'$.

nodes.name: Deterministic and monotonic $\Rightarrow$ straight
nodes.statement: Assume $(X_0,X_1)$ is deterministic and monotonic. Due to the monotonicity, there exists no $x_0$ and $x_0'$ in the support of $\tg_0$, such that $x_0 \neq x_0'$ and $x_{t_0} = x_{t_0}'$ for some $t_0<1$.  This suggests that $X_1-X_0 = \E[X_1-X_0~|~X_t] = v^X(X_t,t)$ for $t\in(0,1)$, and hence  $\d  X_t = (X_1-X_0)\dt = v^X(X_t) \dt $, which is the ODE of the rectified flow. In addition, $X_t$ is obviously the unique solution of this ODE.  Hence $(X_0,X_1)$ is rectifiable and straight following Statement 3 of Theorem~\ref{thm:straightness}.

nodes.name: Take $\xi_t=\xi$ so $V_t=X_t$
nodes.section: 3.5 Denoising Diffusion Models and Probability Flow ODEs
nodes.statement: First, note that we can take $\xi_t = \xi$ for all time $t$, as the correlation structure of $\xi_t$ does not impact the result. Hence, we have $V_t = X_t = \alpha_t X_1 + \beta_t \xi$.

nodes.name: Verify $\dot X_t = \tilde Y_t$
nodes.section: 3.5 Denoising Diffusion Models and Probability Flow ODEs
nodes.statement: To show the equivalence of \eqref{equ:odeobjgg} and \eqref{equ:Lgvphi}, we just need to verify that $\dot X_t = \tilde Y_t$. \bb \tilde Y_t & = -\eta_t X_t + \frac{\sigma_t^2}{2\betatogamma_t^2} ( \alpha_t X_1 - X_t) \\ & = -\dot \eta_t \left ( \alpha_t X_1 + \betatogamma_t \xi \right) + \frac{\sigma_t^2}{2\betatogamma_t}  \xi \\ & = - \dot \eta \alpha_t X_1 + \left ( - \dot \eta_t \betatogamma_t + \frac{\sigma_t^2}{2\betatogamma_t} \right ) \xi \\ & \overset{(*)}{=} \dot \alpha_t X_1 +  \dot \betatogamma_t \xi \\ & = \dot X_t. \ee where in $\overset{(*)}{=}$ we used that $\eta_t = - \frac{\dot \alpha_t}{\alpha_t}$ and $ {\sigma_t^2} = 2\betatogamma_t^2  \left (\frac{\dot\alpha_t}{\alpha_t} -\frac{\dot \betatogamma_t}{\betatogamma_t} \right )$ which can be derived from \eqref{equ:alphadiff}.

nodes.name: Inputs
nodes.statement: \emph{Inputs}: Draws from a coupling $(X_0,X_1)$ of $\tg_0$ and $\tg_1$; velocity model $v_\theta \colon \RR^d \to \RR^d$ with parameter $\theta.$

nodes.name: Training (least-squares fit of $v$)
nodes.statement: \emph{Training}: $\displaystyle \hat \theta = \argmin_\theta \E\left [\norm{X_1 - X_0 - v(t X_1 +(1-t)X_0, ~t )}^2 \right], $ with $t \sim \uniform([0,1])$.

nodes.name: Sampling (ODE simulation)
nodes.statement: \emph{Sampling}: Draw $(Z_0,Z_1)$ following $\d Z_t = v_{\hat\theta}(Z_t,t)\dt$ starting from $Z_0 \sim \tg_0$ (or backwardly $Z_1\sim \tg_1$).

nodes.name: Return flow
nodes.statement: \emph{Return}: $\vv Z = \{Z_t\colon t\in[0,1]\}$.

nodes.name: Reflow (optional)
nodes.statement: \textbf{Reflow} (optional): $\vv Z^{k+1} = \rectifyflow((Z_0^k, Z_1^k))$, starting from $(Z^0_0,Z^0_1) = (X_0,X_1)$.

nodes.name: Distill (optional)
nodes.statement: \textbf{Distill} (optional): Learn a neural network $\hat T$ to distill the $k$-rectified flow, such that $Z^k_1 \approx \hat T(Z^k_0)$.

nodes.name: Initialize Model
nodes.statement: \PyCode{initialize Model}

nodes.name: Loop over data batches
nodes.statement: \PyCode{for x0, x1 in Data:} \PyComment{x0, x1:~samples from  $\tg_0$,  $\tg_1$}

nodes.name: Compute loss and optimizer step
nodes.statement: \PyCode{~~~~Optimizer.zero\_grad()} \\ \PyCode{~~~~t = torch.rand(batchsize)}~~\PyComment{Randomly sample  $t \in$ [0,1]} \\ \PyCode{~~~~\blue{Loss = ( Model(t*x1+(1-t)*x0,~t) - (x1-x0) ).pow(2).mean()}} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Loss.backward()} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Optimizer.step()}

nodes.name: Return Model
nodes.statement: \PyCode{return Model}

nodes.name: Initialize coupling list
nodes.statement: \PyCode{coupling = []}

nodes.name: ODE-solve each $x_0$ and store pair
nodes.statement: \PyCode{for x0, \_ in Data:} \PyComment{x0:~samples from  $\tg_0$ (batchsize$\times$dim)} \\ \PyCode{~~~~x1 = model.ODE\_solver(x0)} \\ \PyCode{~~~~coupling.append((x0, x1))}

nodes.name: Return coupling
nodes.statement: \PyCode{return coupling}

nodes.name: Initialize Coupling = Data
nodes.statement: \PyCode{Coupling = Data}

nodes.name: Iterate Train + sample $K$ times
nodes.statement: \PyCode{for  $k=1,\ldots,K$:} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Model = Train(Coupling)} \\ \PyCode{~~~~Coupling = sample(Model, Data)}

nodes.name: Return Coupling
nodes.statement: \PyCode{return Coupling}
